newsitem.title: UK: Lack of losses push rates lower - Lloyd's agent.
newsitem.headline: Lack of losses push rates lower - Lloyd's agent.

text.p: Insurance rates are still falling and are likely to continue to do so until there is a series of huge individual catastrophe losses, Lloyds of London members' agent Christie Brockbank Shipton Ltd said in its latest newsletter.

"The margins in non-marine catastrophe business between 1993 and 1996 have been too good to miss...There is an inevitable temptation to think that you can reduce the premium if the loss ratio is only 30 percent."
CBSL's market rate index shows marine rates at 116 versus 122 in 1996, non-marine rates at 176 versus 177, aviation at 165 versus 170 and motor at 108 versus 110.
Rates have been declining since a cyclical high in 1994. CBSL uses 1986 as its base year of 100.
Marine underwriters are leading the charge down, CBSL said, with hull rates falling by 15-20 percent in the recent renewal season, while some energy risks have seen cuts of up to 50 percent.

Non-marine insurers are showing slightly better discipline than marine, it said, but rates remain under pressure, noting that Munich Re MUVG F is reported to be competing aggressively for market share "on an international book that would only make money if there were no losses at all."
Aviation rates continue to slide, although airlines that have suffered losses face increases or substantial deductibles.
Motor rates remain under pressure from new arrivals on the UK market.
